summary.intent: Keep making progress on the release-notes plan while the user gets PRs #463 and #464 (stack #465) through the Entire gates and merged.
summary.outcome: Measured likely false-positive noise for the 'not releasing' list, then implemented heading rebase for rich changesets in the PR body on a new branch (feat/rebase-entry-headings). Updated spec, plan and changeset, committed, pushed, and attempted to link the trail and find the new PR number; the result of that step is not shown.

repo: PRs #463 and #464 were blocked by the Entire gates (approval plus an open finding on #464), not by CI; all CI checks on #464 passed.
changed_since_last_tag in crates/callisto-graph/src/changed.rs compares directory tree ids, so reverted edits do not count as changes and it can be reused for the 'not releasing' check.
Between callisto@0.17.0 and 0.18.0 every crate had real src changes, and the fixed group means one changeset covers all crates, so the 'not releasing' check would be quiet on this repo.
Real false positives for 'not releasing' come from tests/, snapshot and markdown-only edits, so a path filter (git diff --name-only with excludes) is needed rather than tree ids alone.
Heading rebase puts the shallowest heading of a change's detail at level 5 and keeps relative depth; fenced and indented code are untouched, and a heading deeper than level 6 becomes a bold line.
The rebase logic lives in crates/callisto-graph/src/changelog/headings.rs and is wired into commands/pr_body.rs, so the changelog can reuse it later.
Project conventions: docs/specs/release.json is the spec, .claude/plans/PLAN-release-notes.md tracks the plan, and each change gets a .changeset/*.md file.
Quality gates used before commit: cargo fmt, cargo clippy -D warnings, RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc, and cargo test -p callisto-graph --lib.

code.finding: New module that rebases markdown headings (## to #####, ### to ######), skips fenced and indented code, and turns headings past level 6 into bold lines.
changed_since_last_tag compares tree ids per directory; a reusable base for the 'not releasing' measurement but not enough alone because it does not filter by path type.

workflow: Use a shell script that builds a rich changeset to check the real binary output end to end, beyond unit tests.
Use /usr/bin/git explicitly and commit with -c commit.gpgsign=false in this environment.
Stacked PRs are linked with `entire trail link <n> --branch <b> --base <parent>`, and the PR number is then looked up with `gh pr list --head`.
Keep the plan file updated as work moves between DONE, IN PROGRESS and TODO, and record measurements in it.

friction: Both PRs were blocked on human approval at the Entire gates, so the user had to act before the stack could merge.
The first run of `cargo test -p callisto-graph --lib` was followed by a rerun with `tail -3`, suggesting the filtered grep output was not informative enough.
The edits were made in the worktree path `.claude/worktrees/macos-15-runners` while the branch was named for a different feature, which may be confusing.
open_items: Merge #463 then #464 (stack #465) once the Entire gates are approved and finding 01M6T6QNY4G4 is resolved.
Add an ignore-paths setting (excluding tests, snapshots and markdown) before enabling the 'not releasing' list.

Step 3b: 'Merging will publish' and the verdict at the top of the PR body, with `callisto version` emitting the preview next to --emit-decision and compose-pr-body reading it (touches CLI, action script and specs).
Markers: `Breaking:` and `Action:` paragraphs feeding the findings list.
Block model remains TODO in the plan.
Reuse headings.rs in the changelog for rich changesets later.
Confirm the new PR for feat/rebase-entry-headings was opened and the trail linked, since the output was not shown.
